status: complete — inputs and outputs both recorded, run is reproducible
role: SECOND cleat geometry. The first (cet_cleat_singleplate_W18x50) closed the flag but rested on one case; its recorded limitation was 'one geometry, one bolt count, one configuration'. This addresses that.
note_on_origin: produced while attempting the GUSSET run — the Connection Setup was still 'Beam To Beam Web', so it is another single plate rather than a brace connection. Useful anyway, and kept.
why_shear_rupture_is_EXACT_here: the module's A36 table is (250, 400) MPa against the exact (248.2, 400.0). Shear rupture depends on Fu alone, and Fu is exact — so the 0.4% residual seen on the A992 case disappears. That is a clean confirmation that the 0.4% there was grade-table rounding and not a formula difference, which was the stated assumption.

elastic_coefficient_check.conclusion: the elastic method is conservative on BOTH geometries, by 3.7% and 10.0%. The margin narrows as the eccentricity falls relative to the bolt group depth, which is the expected behaviour — the two methods converge for a concentric group.

residual: block shear reads 0.6% HIGH on this case with an exact Fu, so it is a small genuine difference in the assumed failure path rather than grade rounding. Below any tolerance that matters, but it is not zero and is recorded rather than rounded away.
